chunks: There is no legal punishment upon a mad person until he regains sanity, nor upon a child until he reaches maturity, nor upon a sleeping person until he wakes up.

key_terms.الصَّبِيِّ: a child who has not yet reached maturity
key_terms.النَّائِمِ: a sleeping person who is presently unaware
key_terms.مَجْنُونٍ: a person who is insane and lacks sound mental capacity
key_terms.يَسْتَيْقِظَ: to awaken and regain conscious awareness
key_terms.يُدْرِكَ: to attain maturity or legal awareness

ai.seo_question: When is a person exempt from legal punishment in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith states that legal punishment is not applied to one who lacks awareness or legal responsibility: the insane person until sanity returns, the child until maturity, and the sleeping person until awakening. It expresses a foundational principle in Islamic jurisprudence that legal accountability depends on the presence of understanding and conscious awareness.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5076 - Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said:
"There is no legal punishment upon a mad person until they regain sanity, nor upon a child until they reach maturity, nor upon a sleeping person until they wake up."
